chapters.title: FutureWorlds
subtitle: A world model predicts future observations from a given action sequence.
We improve the predictor by comparing several candidate futures.

chapters.title: Candidate construction
subtitle: Search starts from shared observations, actions, and task conditions.
A diversity constraint reduces overlap between candidate trajectories.

chapters.title: Candidate-specific memory
subtitle: Each candidate retains its own scene context, state anchors, and recent history.
Generation and policy scoring use the same retained history.

chapters.title: Learning from relative quality
subtitle: Video rewards compare the candidate trajectories with the recorded future.
MemSPO uses group-relative advantages in a search-guided policy update.

chapters.title: RT-1
subtitle: The three sequences show the same future time step.
Compare the can position and its relation to the gripper.

chapters.title: BridgeV2
subtitle: The SFT prediction leaves the pot behind while the gripper moves away.
MemSPO more closely follows the recorded object motion in this example.

chapters.title: RoboCasa
subtitle: Compare the arm and gripper poses as the sequence unfolds.
These are open-loop predictions from recorded trajectories.

chapters.title: Quantitative comparison
subtitle: The reported evaluation covers RT-1, BridgeV2, and RoboCasa.
Full comparisons, protocol details, and code are provided on the project page.
